input.description: Read config and search usages of remoteUrl and cloneRepo

input.command: cat -n src/untracked.ts; cat -n src/store.ts; grep -rn "github" src
input.description: Read untracked and store files, search for github references

input.reason: I read src/git-auth.ts, src/worktree.ts, src/config.ts, src/routes.ts and src/store.ts. At src/git-auth.ts:8, gitAuthArgs checks only `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, and when that passes it returns `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15) calls it with repo.remoteUrl and SERVICE_TOKEN, which comes from process.env.HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN (src/config.ts:4), then runs `git clone` on that same URL. Its only caller is registerRepo (src/routes.ts:19-22). That handler takes remoteUrl straight from req.body and only checks that it is present. Nothing along this path parses the URL or checks the host against an allowlist. Both findings hold.
input.summary: Substring host check in gitAuthArgs leaks service token to lookalike hosts

findings.text: The host check is a substring match, so a remote URL such as `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the service token in an `Authorization` header. Any user who can register a repository can collect the token.
findings.reason: Substring match: src/git-auth.ts:8 is `if (remoteUrl.includes("github.com"))`, and `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` contains that substring, so it passes. Token in an Authorization header: line 9 returns `["-c", `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`]`, and cloneRepo passes SERVICE_TOKEN as the token (src/worktree.ts:15, src/config.ts:4). Any registering user can collect it: registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18-22) reads remoteUrl from req.body, checks only that it is non-empty (`if (!id || !remoteUrl)`), and calls cloneRepo with it. Git then sends the header to the attacker's host.

findings.text: `cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to any host whose URL contains the substring `github.com`.
findings.reason: Passes remoteUrl with the service token: src/worktree.ts:15 is `exec("git", [...gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN), "clone", repo.remoteUrl, dest])`. User-supplied and unvalidated: the only caller, registerRepo (src/routes.ts:19-22), takes remoteUrl from req.body with just a presence check. Any URL containing the substring gets the token: gitAuthArgs uses `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")` (src/git-auth.ts:8), and git clone sends the http.extraHeader to whatever host that URL names.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable credential leak. Any user who can call registerRepo can submit a URL such as https://github.com.evil.example/x.git. The server then sends its GitHub service token (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) as a Bearer header to the attacker's host, and nothing along the path validates the URL.
